Not for redistribution without written consent of Morgan Stanley Morgan Stanley RESEARCH Idea February 5, 2026 07:43 AM GMT Alphabet Inc. | North America What Does This Revenue and Capex Acceleration Mean? GOOGL delivered strong GenAI ROIC signal through GCP and Search, and is stepping up capex substantially. It's Deja Vu from Meta last week. What does this all mean for GOOG, the rest of tech and AMZN? MegaCap Fly Wheels Accelerating to Start '26… GOOGL's accelerating multi-faceted engagement, monetization and capex investment (for further AI-driven innovation and growth) are the second indicator this earnings season (after META's impressive guide) that the leading scaled companies with the most data, reach and ability/willingness to invest are seeing the benefits of their flywheels… and that the gap between them and the smaller players across tech space is likely to widen faster than expected even 35 days ago. Exhibit 1: The flywheels of data, distribution… and investment are all ramping at the MegaCap tech companies as the gap between them and smaller players is widening faster than expected … As AI Productization Driving Accelerated Engagement and Monetization… In 4Q, search grew 17% y/y (150bp faster than us)… with Search's estimated 15.6% y/y ex FX growth the fastest growth in ~4 years (2Q:22) when the Search revenue base was 35% smaller than it is now. Google Cloud grew 48% Y/Y (800bps faster than expected driven by continued breadth of GCP customers for Cybersecurity, data analytics, and Enterprise AI, the latter of which we believe includes AI Infra (GPUs/TPUs) and AI solutions including API usage of Gemini models. Even more impressive (and important for growth durability), the Google Cloud backlog grew 55% q/q adding ~$85bn, reaching approximately ~$240bn. We had written about how GCP could grow 50% here but even we were too low as we now model GCP to grow 71%/51% y/y in '26/'27 and for Google Cloud Segment to grow 61%/46%. Please let us know if interested in our interactive Google Cloud backlog file shown below.

Source: Company data, Morgan Stanley Research estimates … And the Capex/Investment to Drive Deepening Moats: To be clear, GOOGL/ META are investing as GOOGL's '26 capex ($185bn in line with the top end of guide) is now 32% larger than the total data center spend across the 6 largest players only 3 years ago. Even META's $135bn is only ~4% lower than the industry in '23. Note our AMZN capex below is as of 1/13/26 and likely has more upward bias given results so far. Microsoft is covered by Keith Weiss Exhibit 5: We now see Hyperscaler capex approaching $720bn/$900bn in 26/'27… As GOOGL, MSFT and META are all each now expected to spend ~as much/more than total spend in '23 '27 EPS Rises by 3%, PT Unchanged, With Continued Execution Key as FCF Falls ~80% in '27: We raise Search revenue, Cloud revenue, Capex and D&A… as in all our '26/'27 EPS moves by 5%/3%. That said, our higher capex does pressure cash flow materially as our '26/'27 FCF/share falls by 58%/80% to $2.15/$1.48. This, in our view, speaks to the importance that GOOGL continues to execute and productize and monetize its leading corpuses of users and data. Our $330 PT is unchanged, implying paying 24X '27 EPS… while our $415 bull case implies paying 28X our '27 EPS. 3 Reads for AMZN from GOOGL/META/MSFT: 1) Managing Capacity Will Matter: Morgan Stanley Research

Morgan Stanley RESEARCH META's and GOOGL's results showcase how they are spending/budgeting to manage capacity constraints to deliver faster growth in their most important businesses (ads, GCP) even through heavy investment in long-term opportunities. AMZN needs to do the same and deliver 23%+ AWS growth. 2) AWS Backlog Had Better Be Strong and Have Breadth: Growth durability matters to the multiple investors are willing to pay… and in this case the cloud backlogs matter to giving the market more confidence in forward growth of AWS as GCP/Google Cloud are executing at betterthan-expected rates off of high expectations. AMZN management talked to a strong October (likely in part driven by OAI), and we model AWS's backlog to be up 21% ($42bn) q/q in 4Q. 3) Capex Has Upward Bias: We currently model AMZN data center capex of $140bn/$170bn in '26/'27 as it doubles GW capacity. META's and GOOGL's capex (and the rising price of building data centers, memory, etc) only put upward bias on this… which again means revenue will matters to prove the ROIC. OVERWEIGHT THESIS
▪ Continued AI-driven platform-level innovation on Search, YouTube, Cloud, and with other offerings improve con dence in the durability of long term growth. ▪ Continued expense discipline leads to operating leverage and upward revisions on EPS and FCF estimates.

BULL CASE
$415.00
Implied ~16X '27 bull case EBITDA.
Faster innovation and Search/GCP acceleration lead to multiple expansion and higher earnings power. Search revenue accelerates as AI-driven innovation delivers meaningful upside to engagement. New AI offerings prove incremental to the top and bottom line and don't cannibalize core Search. YouTube and Cloud become even bigger contributors to top-line growth, and operate at a higher margin than in our base case.
BASE CASE
$330.00 BEAR CASE
Implied ~14X '27 base case EBITDA.
Assumes pragmatic search revenue growth in '26, continued incremental platform monetization and Google Cloud acceleration in '26. As GOOGL continues platform-level innovation on Search and other categories, we assume pragmatic revenue/EBITDA growth. GOOGL introduces new AI offerings which increase con dence in the durability of long term growth and calm fears around competition. Google Cloud accelerates fidriven by new partnerships and growing backlog.
$200.00
Implied ~8X '27 bear case EBITDA.
Global ad growth slows further and margins face pressure. Assumes slower search advertising growth, and that ad spending slows further. Expense discipline fails to materialize leading to lower than expected margin expansion and adj. EBITDA. New AI products create greater than expected margin pressure due to lower monetization rates and increased compute intensity.
